messages:
jess: FYI customer reported a sudden P95 spike for calls from eu-west-1 -> 700-1200ms starting ~10:12 UTC. They included a trace id. Can someone grab the trace and routing info?

ashok: On it. Trace id? request-id or span id will help.

jess: Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d4e. Customer says header `X-Region: eu-west-1` was set. Example curl they used:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \\n  -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" \\n  -H "X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d4e" \\n  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

maya: Pasted the linked trace from our tracing UI: https://traces.internal/trace/r-0a1b2c3d4e -> top-level route shows ingress eu-west-1 -> router.lookup -> next hop: us-west-2 (weight 1) -> host gw-us-1 -> runtime.

maya: Raw span lines (redacted):
```
span: ingress (region=eu-west-1)
span: smart-router.resolve (selected_route=us-west-2, policy=fallback_on_unhealthy)
span: egress (dst=gw-us-1, ip=52.24.x.x)
span: runtime.generate (node=gw-us-1)
```

liam: :eyes: That looks like a silent failover to us-west-2. Any degrades in eu egress at that time?

nina: Checking SmartRouter health table for eu-west-1 pools... There was a transient 5xx spike on pool eu-gw-2 at 10:11:38 UTC (5 requests, 503) which triggered degraded score for ~30s. Fallback policy is "prefer-local, fallback-any" so it chose us-west-2.

ashok: Can we confirm whether cache/KV or model shard placement forced cross-region? Sometimes model shard unavailable -> route to other region.

maya: Model shards were healthy. Runtime logs show connection established to gw-us-1 with latency 40ms from our fabric, but egress to customer saw extra 600ms due to cross-region roundtrip + peering overhead.

jess: Customer impact: requests that normally p95 ~90ms spiked to 700ms. They asked if requests were routed to wrong region (they expected EU). We should explain failover behavior and mitigation steps.

ashok: Short-term mitigation: force the customer's requests to eu routing by adding `X-Region-Pref: strict` (temporary) or set route pin via account metadata. Longer-term: adjust fallback thresholds so 1-2 503s don't cause cross-region fallback for low-importance traffic.

liam: I'll open an ops ticket to tweak the policy and add a delay window (30s) before cross-region failover for interactive endpoints. Ticket: OPS-4982.

nina: Also adding a tracing annotation to mark when SmartRouter switches region so support can easily filter those traces.

sre-oncall-bot: ALERT: infra-alert: eu-gw-2 503 spike at 2026-11-12T10:11:38Z (5 errors). Correlation: route-fallback events 10:11:39-10:12:05Z.

jess: I'll reply to the customer with timeline + mitigation steps (pin to eu for now). Can someone paste the exact logs we should include for transparency?

maya: Pasting minimal log snippet to include (redacted):
```
2026-11-12T10:11:38Z INFO smart-router: pool eu-gw-2 status=DEGRADED score=0.42 reason=503-spike window=30s
2026-11-12T10:11:39Z INFO smart-router: selected_route=us-west-2 fallback_reason=pool_degraded request_id=r-0a1b2c3d4e
2026-11-12T10:11:39Z INFO egress: connecting dst=gw-us-1 ip=52.24.x.x latency_ms=42
2026-11-12T10:11:40Z INFO runtime: request_complete request_id=r-0a1b2c3d4e total_ms=720 route=us-west-2
```

ashok: Nice. Suggest we also add a short FAQ blurb in Support KB about "Why did my EU traffic route to US?" explaining transient health-based failover and how to pin region. I'll draft.

jess: Thanks all. I'll send to customer and close after they confirm pin worked. :thumbsup:
